legend: In a small town, hidden from prying eyes in the mountains, archaeologists stumbled upon a mysterious cave. Inside, they discovered ancient manuscripts written in an unknown language. After long studies and deciphering the text, the scholars concluded that the records belong to a well-known civilization that existed thousands of years ago and contain information about a certain mathematical problem. They believe that solving this problem may be important for their research, and therefore ask you to write a program to solve it.

The problem is formulated as follows: an array b%%ZSMJ0%% is called bumpy if each of its internal elements (that is, not the first or the last) is strictly greater than or strictly less than both of its neighbors.
Initially, a certain array a%%ZSMJ1%% consisting of integers is given. In one operation, you can choose a certain element of the array and increase or decrease it by 1.
You need to determine the minimum number of operations required to make the array a%%ZSMJ2%% bumpy.
input: The first line of input contains one integer n(3≤n≤105)%%ZSMJ3%% — the length of the array a%%ZSMJ4%%.
The second line contains n%%ZSMJ5%% integers a1,a2,…,an(−109≤ai≤109)%%ZSMJ6%% — the values of the elements of the array a%%ZSMJ7%%.
output: Output the minimum number of operations required to make the array a%%ZSMJ8%% bumpy.
